chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Ibn Muskān who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while he was exiting the Ka'bah, and he was saying 'Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar,' saying it three times. Then he said, 'O Allah, do not exhaust my afflictions, nor let our enemies rejoice in us, for You are the One who causes harm and confers benefit.' Then he descended and prayed beside the stairs, placing the stairs to his left, facing the Ka'bah, with no one between him and it. Then he went out to his house.

key_terms.الدَّرَجَة: The stairs, specifically referring to the stairs of the Ka'bah in this context.
key_terms.الضَّارُّ النَّافِعُ: The One who causes harm and confes benefit, a divine attribute emphasizing God's absolute power.
key_terms.اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ: Allahu Akbar (God is the Greatest), a phrase of glorification often recited during prayer or ritual acts.
key_terms.الْكَعْبَة: The Ka'bah, the cubic structure in Mecca that is the focal point of Islamic prayer.
key_terms.بَلاَئِي: My afflictions or trials, referring to hardships or tests faced by the individual.
key_terms.تُشْمِتْ بِنَا: To make us a cause for rejoicing or triumph for others, specifically enemies.

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say and do when exiting the Ka'bah?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights Imam al-Sadiq’s (AS) specific practice of offering voluntary prayers adjacent to the Ka'bah, a detail that informs the jurisprudential discussion on the preferred location for *Salat al-Tawaf* (prayer after circumambulation). His supplication, 'You are the One who causes harm and bestows benefit,' reflects the Shia theological emphasis on divine omnipotence (*Al-Darr wa al-Nafi*) while seeking protection from the humiliation of enemies during times of affliction. This incident underscores the spiritual significance of the Ka'bah not merely as a physical structure but as a focal point for intimate communion with the Divine.
